current_bottleneck: The clean unified path model preserves support, cross-cell structure, and joint anchor-factor realism, but plain flow-matching MSE still under-allocates conditional probability to realized IV paths, weakens tails, and does not widen in turbulent regimes.
last_result_summary: 647a trained a native joint38 full-future mixed-coordinate path flow. IV score was 4/11: surface, block boundary, IV-EWMA cointegration, and cross-cell correlation passed; coverage, conditionality, time-series, regime coverage, distributional fidelity, mean reversion, and pathwise jump realism failed. Joint audit was strong: factor delta KS mean 0.087, factor KS pass 13/13, factor q99 pass 11/13, factor-factor corr 0.829, IV-factor corr 0.845.
next_step_recommendation: Keep the 647 architecture as the clean native joint baseline and change the objective rather than adding sampling knobs or factor-specific branches. Next principled move: a proper sample-based conditional-law objective for the same path model, so training directly sees multiple generated paths per history and optimizes coverage/tails/path probability rather than only single-target flow MSE.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
